steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A stimulus can be anything: an image, a song, a news story, a poem, an object — it's the starting point for devising.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Research: explore the stimulus from multiple angles — personal, social, historical, political — to find depth.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Brainstorming: generate as many ideas as possible without judging them — quantity leads to quality.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Collaborative creation: everyone contributes — share ideas physically and verbally, build on each other's suggestions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the process you would use to develop a piece of drama from a stimulus. Use a specific example. | How can research enhance a devised piece? What types of research might you do? | Explain how collaborative devising is different from working with a script. What are the challenges and benefits?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Full process: receive stimulus → initial reactions → research → brainstorm → improvise → select strongest ideas → structure → rehearse → refine. Give a specific stimulus example showing each stage. | Research adds depth and authenticity: factual research (statistics, history), personal research (interviews, experiences), artistic research (other plays, art works). It prevents cliches and enriches  | Collaborative: everyone contributes ideas, ownership is shared, multiple perspectives enrich the work. Challenges: compromise, conflicting visions, unequal contribution. Benefits: creativity, investme

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always describe the FULL devising journey — don't just talk about the final piece Show how the STIMULUS led to SPECIFIC dramatic choices In your portfolio, document EVERY stage with evidence Collaborative means shared ownership — show how everyone contributed
